## Install

**Individual integration:** use its **Open in HACS** link below. HACS manages that integration's updates directly.

**One repository for the collection — experimental:** add this catalog to HACS as an **Integration**, download it, and restart Home Assistant. Add **Home Assistant Integration Catalog** under **Settings → Devices & services**, select the integrations you want, then restart again and configure them under their original names.

[![Open catalog in HACS](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/hacs_repository.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/hacs_repository/?owner=seb5594&repository=Home-Assistant-Integrations&category=integration)

The catalog is a custom installer workaround: **HACS manages the installer; the installer manages selected components.**
HACS does not natively install multiple integrations or Git submodules from one repository.
After a catalog update in HACS, restart and open the catalog's **Configure** dialog to apply the new component snapshots, then restart again.
Existing installations from other sources are refused, and deselecting an integration does not uninstall it.

**[Installation, updates, backups and removal →](docs/INSTALL.md)** · **[Deutsche Anleitung →](docs/INSTALL.de.md)** · [HACS repository requirements](https://www.hacs.dev/docs/publish/integration/)

## Source organization

```text
integrations/                         Original repositories, one pinned submodule per integration
custom_components/integration_catalog/
  catalog.json                        Pinned metadata and per-file SHA-256 checksums
  config_flow.py                      Integration selection and explicit installation
  installer.py                        Verified download, ownership checks and backups
assets/brands/                        Source project logos and attribution
docs/                                 Installation and maintenance notes
scripts/sync_catalog.py               Public-source discovery and catalog generation
templates/README.md                   Editable source of this page
```

Submodules are for browsing and development. Users do not need Git or a recursive clone to use the installer.
To work on the sources locally, run `git submodule update --init --recursive` after cloning this repository.

## Support

For a device or integration problem, open an issue in that integration's source repository linked above.
For catalog discovery, installation or backup problems, [open an issue here](https://github.com/seb5594/Home-Assistant-Integrations/issues).
